THE THREE DISHONEST \leanok MARKS DO NOT EXIST: my own published check was the defect

Last session I filed I-0473 reporting three blueprint proofs claiming \leanok while their Lean
carries sorryAx, and made the method point that reading cannot audit this -- only a join against
#print axioms can. The method point stands. The three findings were artifacts of my own join.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, measured over EVERY proof-level mark rather than over this probe's output:
998 proof-level \leanok marks, pinning 1073 declarations, 891 resolvable and probed, ZERO carrying
sorryAx. thm:pic0_smooth and thm:pic0_proper carry no \leanok in either position -- and commit
b61d416e9 says so explicitly, having reverted exactly that kind of withdrawal one run earlier for
exactly the right reason. I reported a defect that a predecessor had already settled correctly.

THE THREE BUGS IN THE PUBLISHED RECIPE, in increasing order of how badly they mislead:

1. It required statement and proof to be TEXTUALLY ADJACENT. Nodes here routinely carry a
   % SOURCE comment block between the two, so 452 of 1311 pinned statement+proof pairs were
   never examined. A check that silently skips a third of its domain reports clean by
   construction.

2. Worse, the non-greedy (.*?) then reaches PAST the true \end{theorem} to find an adjacent
   pair, so it attributes a LATER node's proof to an EARLIER node's statement. That is where
   "thm:pic0_smooth claims a formalised proof" came from: the captured statement spanned nine
   \labels, and the \leanok it found belongs to thm:pic0_geom_irred, which is proved and clean.
   thm:pic0_tangent_space_iso was paired the same way with thm:dual_number_units_split's proof.
   48 nodes mis-attributed.

3. #print axioms on an absent name is an ERROR and lean halts at 100 of them. My first attempt
   at the corrected audit hit that cap and reported "537 probed, 0 leaking" -- which looks like
   a clean result and is a truncated one. The recipe now batches at 40 and ASSERTS the cap was
   not reached, because the failure is silent.

AND THE COVERAGE BOUND THE OLD VERSION NEVER STATED: 143 of the 1073 pins name PRIVATE
declarations, which #print axioms cannot address from outside their file even though they are
genuine checked lemmas (36 in Picard/TensorObjInverse.lean, 21 each in TensorObjSubstrate and
Albanese/AuslanderBuchsbaum). So the honest claim is zero dishonest marks among the 891 probable
pins, and 143 this method cannot decide either way -- not "the blueprint is clean".

The generalisable lesson is not the one I drew last session. I said reading cannot audit a
transitive property, which is true. What this shows is the sharper thing: a mechanical check is
only as good as its DOMAIN, and mine reported on a third of its domain while presenting itself as
exhaustive. Before believing a machine audit, measure what it examined -- and it found nothing
where a human predecessor had already looked and been right.

# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge

A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
the open frontier.

Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.

Two of the committed route's own engines are substantially built.  The rigidified
pushforward gate is **discharged**: `Adelic.instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve` is a real
instance for every curve satisfying the challenge hypotheses, and it measures axiom-clean
at the synthesis site, as do the three extraction theorems that now synthesise it rather
than assuming it.  The finite Galois
quotient has Speiser descent, the affine quotient, and `Γ`-stable affine covers proved;
what remains there is gluing.  Both are stated with proofs and Lean pins in the
blueprint's FGA chapter, §"The Milne–Kollár route".  Neither route is hypothesis-free:
the quotient route needs quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice, the committed route
needs every finite Galois orbit to lie in an affine open, and the same Hironaka example
